subject: health
unitTitle: Substance Misuse Trends, Refusal Skills, and Support Pathways
essentialQuestion: How do I hold a decision when the pressure is quiet, repeated, and from someone close?

prompts.prompt: Explain current substance-misuse trends and why product forms change quickly in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of fentanyl contamination, unknown-supply risk, and naloxone awareness.
Apply impaired driving and passenger decisions in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving refusal under sustained rather than one-time pressure; correct it and explain why.

Connect supporting someone who is using, without taking responsibility for them with treatment, recovery, and confidential support pathways. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a support-pathway map for three fictional situations of escalating seriousness, naming the trusted adult, the service, and the point at which emergency help is called.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The map may be drawn, listed, dictated, or completed on a supplied template. Reading load may be reduced with summarized resource descriptions.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
